$comment: Documentation ownership map. Read by scripts/docs-check-ownership.mjs, which runs in CI.
Each rule says: when a change touches these source paths, it must also touch at least one of
these documents. This is the mechanism that makes prose documentation follow code, rather than
relying on anybody remembering. It is deliberately narrow — it covers the areas where a silent
behaviour change has actually caused an operational problem before, not every file in the repo.
Adding a rule is cheap and is the right response to finding stale documentation. Removing one
needs a reason recorded in the pull request.
Escape hatch: put `docs-exempt: <rule-id> — <reason>` in a commit message when a change genuinely
does not affect the documented behaviour (a rename, a test-only change, a dependency bump). The
reason is required, it is recorded in history, and it is reviewable. Do not use it to defer
documentation you intend to write later.
Generated reference files are NOT listed here. They are covered by the stricter drift check in
scripts/docs-generate.mjs --check, which fails unless they are regenerated exactly.

rules.why: Payment work is frozen and the provider is unchosen. Any change here has to be reconciled against the freeze document in the same pull request, or the freeze silently stops describing reality. The mobile paths are listed because the rule originally covered only Edge Functions, and a change to the app's own payment surface — the Tap WebView, the hosted-checkout handoff, the interrupted-payment recovery — fired no rule at all. A branch took a self-declared 'scoped exception' to the freeze in CheckoutScreen and CI had nothing to say about it. The Moyasar helpers, the shared Tap verify/refund helpers and the two admin readiness panels were added to this rule on 2026-08-24, when a second candidate provider arrived: a change can now be payment-critical without touching a single file with 'tap' in its name, and an admin panel is where an operator points real customers at a gateway.
Push reaches real customers automatically on every order-status transition. A change to dispatch, targeting or consent is a change to live customer messaging.
Sign-in depends on the WhatsApp send hook and the OTP functions. A change that breaks this locks every customer out, so the runbook has to stay accurate.
Orders reach the kitchen through Lazywait. The integration contract and its failure modes are documented because an outage here is invisible in the app but total in the branch.
Deletion is destructive, automated, and legally load-bearing. The runbook and the customer-facing policy have to move together.

A comped customer's every order is free, automatically, with no cap - the highest-abuse surface in the app, and the one where a silent behaviour change is hardest to notice because the customer sees exactly what they expect. The pricing functions live in migrations that are not listed (migrations are append-only and each is its own file), so the rule covers the code that decides WHO is comped and what a comped order looks like to the admin, the customer and the branch.

The confirmation flow spans the app, the POS and the receipt a cashier reads. Its documentation is what makes a customer complaint traceable. The PostgREST transport `supabase/functions/_shared/rest*.ts` was added on 2026-08-30, when order-intake dropped its supabase-js dependency; it is listed because the rule otherwise fires only on the entrypoint, so work that moved order-path behaviour into the shared module and left index.ts untouched would pass the documentation gate in silence.
The watchdog decides when a stranded order raises an alert. Changing its thresholds without saying so leaves operations trusting a number that no longer exists.
The map provider is switchable and its tokens are client-visible. Setup and constraints are documented so the next person does not ship an unrestricted key.
The one-time-code field carries platform-specific autofill behaviour that took a long investigation to establish. Changing it without updating the findings invites repeating that investigation.
There is more than one path to production and only one of them is meant to be active. A workflow change that adds a second deploy path must be visible in the deployment documentation.
